title: ABM software pricing 2026: 6sense, Demandbase and more
summary: What ABM software costs in 2026: 6sense, Demandbase, Terminus, AdRoll ABM (RollWorks) and UserGems compared, with sources and contract terms.
body_markdown:
**ABM software in 2026 costs anywhere from about $10,000 to well over $150,000 a year.** Based on Vendr purchase data, the median buyer pays about $54,250 a year for 6sense, $65,301 for Demandbase and $23,275 for Terminus. UserGems publishes its prices ($40,000, $75,000 and $150,000 a year), while 6sense, Demandbase and AdRoll ABM (formerly RollWorks) quote every deal.


The sticker price is only part of the bill. Contract length, renewal uplifts, implementation fees and how much of your TAM you can cover decide what you actually pay. Here’s what each vendor costs, what drives the number up, and how to compare quotes fairly.


### How much does ABM software cost? The quick comparison


The figures below come from vendor pricing pages where they exist, and from Vendr’s anonymized purchase data where they don’t. Vendr medians move as new deals land, so check the live page before you quote them in a budget.


**6sense**


- Pricing model: custom quote; modules plus data credits
- Typical cost: median $54,250 a year; range $11,143 to $131,490 across 322 purchases (Vendr, Nov 2026). Larger deployments with ads and wide TAM coverage go higher.
- Contract length: typically 12 to 24 months; multi-year deals are common at enterprise level
- What drives cost: modules (advertising, conversational email, sales intelligence), credits, TAM size and renewal uplifts


**Demandbase**


- Pricing model: a platform fee plus a flat fee per user (Demandbase pricing page)
- Typical cost: median $65,301 a year; range $21,845 to $161,475 across 164 purchases (Vendr, Nov 2026)
- Contract length: buyers report 12-, 15- and 24-month terms (Vendr community notes)
- What drives cost: platform fee, number of users, and advertising and data add-ons


**Terminus (now part of DemandScience)**


- Pricing model: custom quote
- Typical cost: median $23,275 a year; range $10,718 to $65,424 across 67 purchases (Vendr, Nov 2026)
- Contract length: not published, so confirm it in your quote
- What drives cost: ad spend and channels, and the number of target accounts


**AdRoll ABM (formerly RollWorks)**


- Pricing model: quote-based packages (Account-Based Advertising, ABM + Advertising, ABM). Account-Based Retargeting has no platform fee; you pay for media (AdRoll pricing page).
- Typical cost: no public list price, and no reliable third-party median
- Contract length: not published, so confirm it in your quote
- What drives cost: package, media spend and managed services


**UserGems**


- Pricing model: published annual packages with credits and unlimited users (usergems.com/pricing)
- Typical cost: Core $40,000 a year, Advanced $75,000 a year, Elite $150,000 a year, plus one-time implementation of $3,000 to $10,000. Enterprise is priced on request.
- Contract length: annual packages
- What drives cost: credits, TAM coverage (2,000 to 10,000+ accounts) and package features


### What does 6sense cost?


6sense doesn’t publish prices. According to[Vendr’s 6sense pricing data](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/6sense) , the median buyer pays $54,250 a year, with deals from about $11,000 to $131,000. Buyers save about 17% on average through negotiation.


What pushes 6sense up: add-on modules, data credits that run out mid-year, TAM expansion and renewal uplifts. 6sense also retired its free Sales Intelligence plan in August 2026, so every evaluation now runs through sales. We break down each cost component in our[6sense pricing breakdown](https://www.usergems.com/6sense-limitations/6sense-pricing-breakdown-is-it-worth-the-investment) , and the contract terms to watch in[6sense cost, pricing transparency and contract lock-in](https://www.usergems.com/blog/6sense-cost-pricing-transparency-and-contract-lock-in) .


**Where 6sense earns its price:** large enterprise teams with RevOps capacity, a mature ABM program and a need for account-level intent, advertising and orchestration in one contract.


### What does Demandbase cost?


Demandbase is the one enterprise ABM vendor that explains its model on its own pricing page: a platform fee covering the core software and services, plus a flat fee per user. You still need a quote for the number.[Vendr’s Demandbase data](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/demandbase) puts the median at $65,301 a year, with average savings of about 13%.


Contract structures vary more than you’d expect. Vendr’s community notes include a 12-month deal with a 3% renewal cap, a 24-month commitment with an extra renewal discount, and a 15-month term with an opt-out after three months. Those are the terms to ask for.


**Where Demandbase earns its price:** enterprise teams that want B2B advertising, account intelligence and sales-facing insights in one suite, and want per-user pricing they can model.


### What does Terminus cost?


Terminus merged with DemandScience in late 2024 and now sells as part of an account-based demand generation offer. It’s the lowest-cost of the classic ABM suites in Vendr’s data, with a median of $23,275 a year ([Vendr](https://vendr.com/marketplace/terminus) ) and deals between about $10,700 and $65,400.


**Where Terminus fits:** teams that mainly want account-based advertising and web personalization without an enterprise intent contract. Before you sign a multi-year deal, ask how the DemandScience merger affects the roadmap and packaging.


### What does RollWorks (AdRoll ABM) cost?


RollWorks is now AdRoll ABM. The old RollWorks pricing page redirects to AdRoll, which lists four ABM packages. Three are quote-based. The fourth, Account-Based Retargeting, has no fee to get started; you pay only for media.


That makes AdRoll ABM the easiest entry point if your ABM program is mostly ads. Third-party price estimates for RollWorks conflict with each other, so get a written quote rather than relying on a blog number.


**Where AdRoll ABM fits:** smaller B2B teams starting ABM with retargeting and account-based display, especially if they already run AdRoll.


### What does UserGems cost?


UserGems publishes its pricing. There are three annual packages, all with unlimited admin and end users:


- **Core, $40,000 a year:** list building, Scoring, automated campaigns, the Gem-E Writing Agent and Gem-E Research Agent, the AI Chrome Extension, and CRM and sales engagement integrations. TAM coverage of 2,000 to 4,000 accounts.
- **Advanced, $75,000 a year:** adds the UserGems MCP, ad audience sync and ad platform integrations. 4,000 to 10,000 accounts.
- **Elite, $150,000 a year:** adds contact-level intent, website deanonymization, Buying Stages and CRM hygiene. 10,000+ accounts.


One-time implementation runs $3,000 to $10,000 depending on package. Full details are on the[UserGems pricing page](https://www.usergems.com/pricing) .


The comparison that matters is what you get for the money. UserGems is the AI command center for outbound and ABM. The UserGems Live Identity Graph keeps every account and contact that matters to you up to date, scores them with a custom model built on your own wins and losses, and pushes campaigns into the CRM, sales engagement, marketing automation and ad tools you already use. Your SEP still sends the emails and your ad platforms still serve the ads.


### What drives ABM software cost up?


Across every vendor, the same five things move the number:


1. **TAM size.** Most vendors price on how many accounts you track. Expanding mid-contract usually triggers a new order form.
2. **Modules and add-ons.** Advertising, conversational email and sales seats are often separate line items on 6sense and Demandbase quotes.
3. **Credits.** Data and AI actions run on credits at 6sense and UserGems. Ask what happens when you run out.
4. **Contract length and uplifts.** Multi-year terms get bigger discounts and less flexibility. Renewal uplifts of 5% to 10% are common unless you cap them.
5. **People cost.** The license is the visible part. The RevOps time it takes to configure, maintain and interpret an enterprise ABM suite is the hidden part.


### How to compare ABM software quotes fairly


List prices tell you little because the packages differ so much. Normalize every quote to three numbers:


- **Cost per covered account per year.** Divide the annual fee by the accounts you can actually track and act on.
- **Cost per named buyer.** Account-level intent tells you a company is researching. Contact-level signals tell you who. If your reps need names, price the work it takes to get from one to the other.
- **Total cost of ownership over the full term.** License, implementation, renewal uplifts, add-ons and the headcount needed to run it.


Then ask what turns into pipeline. An ABM program that reaches 3X the volume of accounts with the same team, or cuts a four-week process to about two, changes the math more than a 15% discount does. ### Frequently asked questions


#### What is the cheapest ABM software?


For ad-led ABM, AdRoll ABM’s Account-Based Retargeting has no platform fee; you pay for media. Among full ABM suites, Terminus has the lowest median in Vendr’s data at about $23,275 a year. Cheapest rarely means best value, so compare cost per covered account and cost per named buyer.


#### Is 6sense more expensive than Demandbase?


Not on median. Vendr data shows a $54,250 median for 6sense and $65,301 for Demandbase, though 6sense deals with advertising and wide TAM coverage can run higher. Your quote depends on modules, users and TAM size. See[UserGems vs 6sense](https://www.usergems.com/usergems-vs-6sense) for how the approaches differ.


#### Which ABM vendors publish their pricing?


UserGems publishes package prices. Demandbase explains its model (a platform fee plus a per-user fee) without listing numbers. 6sense, Terminus and AdRoll ABM’s core packages are quote-only.


#### How long are ABM software contracts?


Most run 12 months, with 24-month terms common at enterprise level. Shorter terms, opt-out windows and renewal caps are all negotiable, so ask for them before you sign, while you still have leverage.


#### Do ABM platforms charge implementation fees?


Usually. UserGems lists a one-time fee of $3,000 to $10,000. Enterprise ABM suites often price implementation and professional services separately, so get that number in writing.


### See what your budget actually buys


If you’re comparing ABM quotes this quarter, look past the license. Ask which accounts are in market, which people at those accounts to reach, and how fast that turns into pipeline.
